newsitem.title: UK: Mediterranean crude rallies as sweet margins soar.
newsitem.headline: Mediterranean crude rallies as sweet margins soar.

text.p: Mediterranean crude oil markets extended their rally on Thursday as refinery margins soared, especially for sweet distillate-rich grades, traders said.
Tunisian Zarzaitine, having traded last week at Dated Brent +70 cents, was now on offer at Dated +75, and Algeria raised the October price of its Saharan Blend by nine cents to Dated +70.

A growing volume of West African crude was heading into Europe, both in the north and the Mediterranean, as Med refining margins were particularly strong, especially for refiners producing the new 0.05 percent sulphur European diesel.
"One or two Forcados cargoes have been sold at Dated +50/55 cents, and most people expect it to get stronger," said a Nigerian equity holder.
There were market rumours of at least one end-October Forcados sold by a trader on Wednesday at Dated +54/55 cents, but this was not confirmed.

"If you are bullish middle distillates, and most people are, we could see Forcs bounding up in the Med. It appears all the barrels are ending up in the Med and going to the States. There's been nothing to the Far East in October," he added.
Other rumours pointed to a mid-October Bonny Light/Medium cargo sold on Wednesday at Dated +49/40 cents.
Trades were typically kept quiet because dealers did not want to reveal the true strength of the market just as Nigeria's NNPC was setting its prices for October.

Sour crude in the Mediterranean was steady and very thin as most Russian Urals was sold out and Syrian prices were not yet set for October. A large Sept 27-29 Urals was rumoured to have been sold at Dated Brent -80 cents c+f Augusta.

Sytrol on Thursday repeated its offer of Dated Brent -30 cents for Syrian Light crude liftings in October, 10 cents above September, but buyers said they could not accept this price. Buyers said they were hoping for a rollover of September prices at the very least.
Sytrol lowered its offer of the heavy Souedie crude from Dated Brent -$2.85 to $2.90 on Thursday, but buyers were looking for a discount of more than $3.00 for October liftings.
